title: Screens and Our Health: 5 Ways to Protect Our Brains and Bodies
body_text: Author: Devika Bhushan, MD These days, as young people all over the world start a new school year, phone-free school days are more common than ever and the call for a screen-aware existence is spreading rapidly. Even if this is not the norm (yet) in your school community, there are important steps you can take today to make your family’s or community’s relationships with screens healthier — for better health, connections, and learning. Here’s the backdrop: US Surgeon General Vivek Murthy, MD, MBA, issued an advisory in 2023 about the impacts of social media on children and teens , and a more recent call in 2024 for warning labels on social media , given the known health harms and a dearth of data on longer-term impacts. Research also shows that eliminating phones during times of focus, like during the school day, benefits both learning and health. For instance, in Norway, middle schools that banned cell phones had higher grades and a nearly 60% lower need for specialty care, including for mental health needs, in girls, and 40-50% less bullying reported for all kids, compared to schools that didn’t. Many schools have since jumped on this bandwagon, requiring students to either leave phones in lockers or lock them in a Yondr pouch through the school day, with positive impacts. Florida , Utah , Indiana , and South Carolina have all restricted phone use for students in schools at a state-wide level, with California likely to, starting in 2026. And at the local level, this summer, Los Angeles , the nation’s second largest school district, became the largest district in the US to enact a district-wide phone use restriction, to start in January 2025. Nick Melvoin, Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) School Board member who spearheaded this resolution, notes the zeitgeist really changed with the recent publication of the widely read book, The Anxious Generation , by Jonathan Haidt, about the dangers of a ‘phone-based childhood.’ “I do see a rare area of bipartisanship,” said Melvoin. “You see states like Florida and now states like California — those Governors agree about almost nothing — but this is one of them.” The ultimate hope is to have students develop healthier habits “that will benefit them as they become adults — when they will have to have a healthy relationship with technology without policies that restrict their phone use,” shared Smita Malhotra, MD, Chief Medical Director for LAUSD. “We are hoping this policy will help create healthier learning environments for children and foster more meaningful in-person interactions that nurture their social-emotional development.” She noted that district-provided laptops and tablets will still be used, and schools will open up access to universal mental health screening and tools like therapy as needed. ____________________________ If you are a caregiver, student, or staff at a school where phones are still present in learning spaces, stay tuned — these changes may come to you sooner than you know. To advocate for these changes in your community, use these guidelines . In the meantime, here are some rules of thumb you can apply as a family or school to help protect learning and health. 1) Create a collective norm around delaying smartphones and social media use in your community. Collectively normalize delaying access to smartphones and to social media accounts in your caregiving and school communities. This makes it easier for youth to stick to these norms without feeling left out. For example, you might decide to delay smartphones until high school and start kids off instead with phones that can’t surf the Internet or have apps — and can only call and text. ‍ 2) Parents and caregivers: intentionally model healthy tech behaviors. As a family, designate certain screen-free zones and activities, like meals and focus time. ‍ Research shows that young peoples’ screen time habits often mirror those of their caregivers. So any change a youth makes has to start with the adults in the family. A 2023 survey found that 9 in 10 (89%) Americans check our phones within the first 10 minutes of waking up, and nearly 6 in 10 (57%) consider ourselves “addicted” to phones. “Technoference” — when devices distract caregivers from being present and responsive with kids — is an increasing issue these days. In one recent Canadian study , parents of preschoolers (ages 3-5) were distracted by devices an average 12-16 times per day. This was associated with children scoring lower on emotional self-regulation and higher on externalizing and internalizing mental health symptoms. A recent Pew survey found that nearly half of teens say their parent is at least sometimes distracted by a phone when trying to talk with them. So it’s up to us adults to do the hard work of identifying and modifying our own relationships with screens in tandem with helping our kids do the same. ‍ Choose times to connect as a family free of devices. For example, you might make family meals or walks and any key focus times (like doing homework) screen-free zones to enable everyone to be maximally present. Invest in fun, real world alternatives to screens like regular time in nature, family dance parties, or game nights. When designating phone-free zones, you’ll get the best results from leaving phones in another room. Just having a phone out on a table, even when powered off and not being used, siphons off our attentional resources , compared to leaving it another room — making it harder for us to pay full attention to an important conversation or our homework. (These effects are strongest for those of us most dependent on our phones.) ‍ 3) Remove devices from bedrooms, or at least place them far from beds. Along with mealtime use, bedtime screen use is associated with more problematic youth social media, video game, and mobile phone use overall, and also with sleep problems , including trouble falling or staying asleep and disturbances through the night. This is partially mediated by exposure to blue light from screens (and other artificial light sources) that signal to our brains that it’s daytime, suppressing the sleep-inducing hormone melatonin and related functions. For optimal sleep, set a goal to be off your device at least 1-2 hours before your desired bedtime. At bedtime, dim the lights, make the room cool, and consider wearing blue light-blocking glasses , which protect your brain from large doses of daytime-signaling blue light. These steps can help boost your natural drive to sleep by ensuring timely production of melatonin and related nighttime functions. Once that phone is out of reach, I urge you to find alternative ways to wind down to boost sleep quality. Maybe it’s reading a book, journaling, doing stretches, smelling lavender, or mindful breathing — pick something soothing that you enjoy and can return to night after night to powerfully cue your brain to switch into unwinding and resting. For bonus points, rig up an old-school alarm clock (rather than one on your phone, even across the room) so you’re not looking at your device first thing in the morning, either. ‍ 4) Make devices boring and less accessible. ‍ Experiment with making your phone a less easy source of dopamine hits. Turn off notifications; turn your phone to grayscale; leave your phone on airplane mode — or at home — for an afternoon to see what this opens up. (Simply switching a smartphone to grayscale reduced screen time by 18% in one study . Here are instructions for how to set that up.) ‍ 5) Mindfully choose higher-quality content, and make it harder to consume low-quality or harmful content. Not all screen content or practices around consumption are created equal. For example, in preschool-age children, co-viewing an educational show like Daniel Tiger with caregivers can actually improve social-emotional outcomes like emotional regulation, while lower-quality or age-inappropriate content can harm. When we do use screens, intentionality about higher-quality use is the key. Identify the kinds of screen time that make each family member feel better (as opposed to worse) after consumption, and make time-bound goals for use. Also have each member of the family delete the apps or activities that most steal focus off device(s), creating more friction around their use. You might designate limited times to engage them — from a computer instead of a phone. For instance, I’ve deleted my work email and a key social media app from my phone, and I designate specific times in my day to check in and reply to any messages from a computer. This works well for me because I’m only on my computer during the work day, but have my phone on me at other times. So I’ve made social media and email a part of my working hours, and eliminated their presence from my downtime — an incredible upgrade. ____________________________ ‍ I wish your family and community all the best in your journey to reclaim screen-free presence in the real world and better health — it’s definitely not easy, and it’s definitely worth the ongoing effort. ____________________________ Devika Bhushan, MD, is Daybreak’s Health’s Chief Medical Officer. She is a pediatrician and public health leader with expertise in trauma-informed systems, health equity, mental health, and stress and resilience. She shares actionable insights for well-being at Ask Dr Devika B . ‍

title: Native API vs. Generated API: Which Is Right for Your Integration Stack?
summary: When a platform publishes an official API, you use it. When it doesn't, you either build something fragile or you use a generated API — and those two paths have very different maintenance profiles in production.
body_text: Three weeks before GA, your product needs to pull patient records from a regional EHR that serves your target hospital network. Someone opens the API docs and finds a read-only reporting endpoint that covers maybe 30% of what you need. For the rest, there's no public API. The platform was built for browser-based workflows and no one at the vendor has built a developer API for external use. The question isn't whether to integrate. The question is whether you're doing it with a native API, a generated API, or a browser automation tool that will break the first time the EHR ships a redesign. Native API integration and generated API integration both provide programmatic access to platforms. They solve different problems, live in different parts of the stack, and have very different maintenance profiles once they're in production. This post breaks down where each one belongs. What is a native API? A native API is an interface officially designed, documented, and maintained by the platform that owns the underlying system. It follows versioned, stable contracts, ships with an official SDK, and carries explicit support commitments from the vendor. Stripe, Twilio, and Salesforce are the canonical examples: well-documented endpoints, backward-compatible versioning, published rate limits, and dedicated developer relations teams. When a platform publishes a native API, it controls the contract. Breaking changes go through deprecation cycles. New endpoints get changelog entries. Your integration is building against something the platform wants you to depend on. That stability is the core value. The platform is aligned with you: their API's reliability is their product. What is a generated API? A generated API is a production-ready API built against a platform's private network layer (the same HTTP requests the platform's own frontend makes) rather than against an officially published interface. It provides equivalent programmatic access when no native API exists. Integuru builds generated APIs by authenticating into a target platform, mapping its internal network requests, and producing a documented API with the same inputs, outputs, and operations you'd expect from a native integration. The result is an API endpoint your code can call as if the platform had published one itself. The distinction matters: this is not web scraping. Integuru communicates at the HTTP layer, below the rendered UI, which means UI changes on the platform's frontend don't break the integration. The underlying request structure is more stable than the DOM. When native APIs are the right choice Use a native API when the platform has published one and it covers the operations you actually need. The conditions that make native APIs the clear choice: The platform maintains versioning. APIs like Stripe's guarantee backward compatibility within a major version. You can upgrade your integration on your schedule, not the platform's. The API covers your full operation set. If you need to create a payment intent, retrieve a customer, and issue a refund, and all three endpoints exist, you're done. The platform publishes rate limits and SLAs. Stripe publishes its rate limit tiers. Twilio publishes uptime commitments. You can design your retry logic and queue depth against documented numbers. Official SDKs reduce integration overhead. When Stripe ships a Python or Node SDK, your integration is tested against the same library thousands of other developers are using. If your stack includes Stripe for payments, Twilio for messaging, or Salesforce for CRM, native APIs are the correct choice in every case. They're well-resourced, well-documented, and actively maintained. Where native APIs fall short The problem is that most platforms your product needs to integrate with are not Stripe. The majority of platforms that power real business workflows: EHR systems, TMS platforms, government portals, legacy SaaS tools in healthcare and logistics. Most have no public API at all, or an API that covers only a fraction of the operations they actually support. The gaps appear in several patterns: The platform has no public API. Healthcare EHR systems like eClinicalWorks, logistics TMS platforms, and most government portals were built for browser-based workflows. There is no API to call because the vendor never built one for external use. The API exists but doesn't cover the operation you need. Some platforms publish read-only APIs for reporting while keeping write operations locked to their UI. If you need to submit a claim, update a patient record, or dispatch a shipment, the native API won't help. Rate limits are too restrictive for your throughput. Some platforms impose limits that work for casual integrations but break under the volume that production operations require. The certification process is prohibitive. Formal API partnership programs require months of application review and enterprise contract minimums, a timeline that rarely fits the window between signing a customer and shipping the integration. This is where a generated API fills the gap. How generated APIs compare to native APIs in production The honest comparison across the dimensions that matter for production systems: Dimension Native API Generated API (Integuru) Documentation Published by the vendor; versioned changelog Integuru-generated docs; equivalent coverage of supported operations Stability Versioned contracts; deprecation notices HTTP-layer stability; less exposed to UI changes than browser automation Maintenance Vendor handles breaking changes Integuru 24/7 on-call team handles endpoint drift and auth changes Rate limits Published by vendor; predictable Platform-dependent; Integuru monitors and surfaces limits as discovered Write operations Vendor-controlled; may be read-only Supports full read/write operations the platform UI exposes Platform coverage Only platforms that chose to build a public API Any authenticated web platform Table reflects Integuru production plans. Updated July 2026. Native APIs hold one structural edge: versioned stability. When a vendor publishes a deprecation notice six months in advance, you have a runway to update on your own schedule. Generated APIs don't have that guarantee. What they have instead is maintenance-as-a-service: Integuru's on-call team handles endpoint drift so your engineering team doesn't carry that overhead. For the 90% of platforms that never published a native API in the first place, this is the only path that isn't "build it yourself and fix it forever." The honest position: if a platform has a well-resourced native API that covers your operations, use it. If it doesn't, a generated API isn't a compromise. It's the correct tool for the problem. How Integuru generates APIs for platforms without native APIs Integuru builds a generated API by mapping a platform's private network layer, then delivering a documented API endpoint your code calls directly via HTTP. The process works in four steps: Authentication. You connect a platform by entering its domain and completing an auth flow, including 2FA where required. This takes roughly 10 minutes. Network mapping. Integuru's agent captures the HTTP requests the platform makes for the operations you need, mapping inputs, outputs, and branching logic across real-world account states. API generation. Within 10 to 20 minutes, you receive production-ready endpoints with full input schema documentation. Maintenance. Integuru's 24/7 on-call team monitors for endpoint drift and handles auth changes automatically, so your integration doesn't break when the platform updates its internal structure. The result performs on the metrics that matter for production: 99.9%+ reliability rate Under 3 seconds average response time Direct HTTP: no browser automation, no Puppeteer, no Selenium in the path Because Integuru communicates below the UI layer, the integration is substantially more stable than a browser-based approach. A platform redesigning its frontend doesn't touch the HTTP layer your integration depends on. Mixing native and generated APIs in an integration stack Most production stacks end up using both. Native APIs where platforms offer them; generated APIs for the long tail of platforms that don't. A realistic architecture pattern looks like this: Payments via Stripe native API. Stripe publishes a mature, versioned API with official SDKs. Use it as designed. Your payments integration benefits from official versioning, published rate limits, and extensive community support. Messaging via Twilio native API. Same reasoning. Twilio's API surface covers every operation you need at the throughput your product requires. Clinical data via Integuru-generated EHR API. Your target EHR (whether it's eClinicalWorks, ModMed, or a regional system) has no public API for the write operations your product needs. Integuru generates the API, handles auth complexity including 2FA, and maintains the integration so you don't absorb that overhead. The pattern generalises: native APIs for well-resourced platforms that chose to publish them; Integuru-generated APIs for everything else your product depends on. This isn't a fallback architecture. It's the realistic shape of any integration stack that reaches past the top 20 SaaS tools into the specific platforms your customers' workflows actually run on. title: Best Employbridge Alternatives and Competitors in 2026
summary: Compare the best Employbridge alternatives and competitors for temporary staffing, shift coverage, and hiring. See how Instawork compares with agencies, staffing platforms, and job boards.
body_text: If you are comparing the best Employbridge alternatives and competitors, start with the option that can fill shifts fast, keep show rates high, and give you more control over labor costs. Instawork stands out for businesses that need temporary, seasonal, long-term temporary, and full-time hiring support through one platform. Other options include traditional staffing agencies, online staffing platforms, and job boards, but each comes with tradeoffs in speed, worker quality, and hands-on management. If you want a quick overview of staffing platform options, review this guide to on-demand staffing apps . Best Employbridge Alternatives and Competitors Instawork Trustpilot Rating: 3.9 Instawork is a strong Employbridge alternative for businesses that need speed, reliability, and flexibility. Businesses can post shifts for temporary workers, long-term temporary workers, and full-time hiring in one place. The platform has access to more than 10 million vetted local workers across the U.S. and Canada. Instawork reports fill rates above 90%, compared with an industry average of 50% to 60%. Shifts can be filled in as little as two hours and often within 24 hours. Businesses also benefit from a worker show rate above 98%, automated clock-in and clock-out with geofencing, and a repeat worker experience businesses often want to keep. This makes Instawork a better fit than many traditional agencies when labor demand changes quickly. Find reliable workers fast Skip the endless screening. We source, vet, and place dependable workers who are ready to start when you need them. Find Qualified Workers Adecco Adecco is a large staffing agency with broad coverage across industries and role types. It can be a useful option for businesses that want a traditional agency relationship and support for office, industrial, and professional hiring. Compared with platform-based options, the process may feel less self-serve and less immediate for shift-based staffing needs. Businesses that need local scale may consider Adecco, but those prioritizing faster shift fulfillment and direct scheduling control may prefer Instawork. Randstad Trustpilot Rating: 2 Randstad is another major staffing firm serving industrial, administrative, and professional hiring needs. It is often considered by businesses looking for a national provider with recruiting support. As with many traditional firms, service can be effective for planned hiring but less suited for urgent shift coverage. If your operation depends on filling roles within hours rather than days, a marketplace model like Instawork may offer more predictable speed. Manpower Manpower is a long-standing staffing agency used by employers across light industrial, clerical, and administrative roles. It can work well for businesses that want agency-led recruiting and screening. Compared with digital staffing platforms, visibility into worker ratings, repeat performance, and shift-level control may be more limited. Businesses that care about rebooking proven workers may find Instawork more operationally efficient. PeopleReady PeopleReady focuses on on-demand and temporary labor, especially in construction, events, hospitality, and general labor. It may appeal to employers with day-to-day staffing needs. Businesses comparing PeopleReady with Instawork should look closely at worker quality controls, scheduling experience, and repeat staffing. Instawork offers worker ratings after each shift and reports that businesses ask for the same workers to return 93% of the time. Wonolo Trustpilot Rating: 2.6 Wonolo is a staffing platform built for flexible labor and shift-based work. It is often compared with Instawork for warehouse, events, and general labor staffing. Businesses deciding between the two should compare fill speed, worker show rate, and quality controls. Instawork highlights daily worker skill assessment calls, a large vetted network, and strong trust and safety performance, which can matter when reliability is the top priority. Bluecrew Bluecrew offers W-2 staffing support for warehouses, logistics, and other hourly operations. It may be a fit for businesses that prefer a more managed labor model. Compared with Instawork, some employers may find role coverage and labor flexibility differ based on market and job type. If your staffing needs span seasonal shifts, long-term temporary projects, and direct hiring, Instawork offers broader hiring paths through one system. Upwork Trustpilot Rating: 3.9 Upwork is a freelance marketplace, not a traditional staffing agency. It is best for remote project work rather than local hourly labor. Businesses searching for an Employbridge alternative for warehouses, hospitality, or in-person operations will usually need a platform designed for local shift staffing. Instawork is built for those use cases, while Upwork is better suited for digital and knowledge-based projects. Indeed Indeed is a job board and hiring marketplace used for permanent and hourly roles. It gives employers broad reach but often requires more internal effort to screen, schedule, and manage applicants. title: Aerospace Compliance Without the Headaches: Fluids, Specs, and OEM Approvals Explained
summary: Aerospace fluid compliance refers to ensuring metalworking and process fluids meet regulatory, OEM, and program-specific requirements without disrupting production. For aerospace quality, EHS, supply chain, and manufacturing leaders, that typically means k
body_text: Aerospace fluid compliance refers to ensuring metalworking and process fluids meet regulatory, OEM, and program-specific requirements without disrupting production. For aerospace quality, EHS, supply chain, and manufacturing leaders, that typically means keeping fluid selection , documentation, and process controls aligned so audits do not turn into schedule disruptions. Why aerospace compliance keeps getting harder Aerospace compliance is getting harder because regulations and customer flow-down requirements keep expanding, increasing the documentation and traceability needed to stay audit-ready. Increasing EHS and chemical-management requirements : These requirements can change what documentation needs to be current and accessible (for example, SDS access and internal restricted-substance screening where applicable). More OEM flow-downs per program : These flow-downs often require tighter requirement mapping to show that the exact fluid in use aligns to the customer program, specification, or approved list the site follows. The hidden cost of non-approved fluids Using non-approved fluids can create hidden costs— requalification work, audit findings, and program delays—that quickly outweigh any short-term purchasing or availability benefits. Requalification work : Extra trials, updated work instructions, and added inspection to show a change won’t negatively affect surface finish or downstream compatibility. Audit findings : Documentation gaps or unclear traceability can trigger nonconformances and corrective-action workload during customer or third-party audits. Program delays : Teams may pause purchasing or production while requirements are verified and supporting evidence is gathered, which can push delivery dates. What aerospace auditors actually look for Aerospace auditors look for process control, traceability, and documented alignment to requirements not performance claims about a fluid. In practice, audit readiness depends on being able to show the exact product in use, where it is used, and how it is controlled for. Requirement mapping documentation : Evidence showing how the exact product in use aligns to the customer program, specification, or approved list the site follows (including revision/date where applicable). Restricted-substance screening records (where applicable) : Supporting documentation used for internal reviews and customer questions about restricted chemistry. Traceability and SDS access : Records that identify the product (name/SKU) and provide current Safety Data Sheets and supporting technical documents. Process control records : Defined targets (for example, concentration), a monitoring cadence, and documented corrective actions that demonstrate process stability. Why pre-approved fluids matter In aerospace contexts, “pre-approved” fluids are products already qualified to an OEM list, customer specification, or internal quality standard for a defined use. Reduced documentation burden : Fewer ad hoc document requests and less last-minute evidence gathering during internal reviews and customer audits. Faster program onboarding : Standardized fluids can reduce variation across work centers and simplify training and rollout across multiple aerospace programs. More consistent audit performance : Clear product identity, accessible documentation, and defined controls support repeatable audit readiness. Pre-approval reduces compliance risk by removing ambiguity about what is acceptable for a defined use. Pre-approval (or prior qualification) also supports standardization across cells and sites. When evaluating metalworking fluids for machining and grinding, organizations may start their review with products such as HOCUT® 795 B and QUAKERCOOL® 8013 , then validate fit against specific program requirements and internal controls. How to audit your current fluid portfolio This audit is typically owned jointly by quality and EHS, with input from manufacturing and supply chain to confirm what is actually used on the floor. A review is commonly performed at least annually and whenever a major program change, customer requirement change, or product change is introduced. Organizations aiming to reduce compliance risk without creating unnecessary friction in production can start with a simple internal audit of current fluid usage. The purpose is not to rewrite the entire process; it is to close the gaps that tend to surface during customer reviews: inconsistent naming, missing SDS access, unclear program fit, or undefined control practices. What to look for A basic internal audit should confirm five things: inventory accuracy, documentation access, program alignment, control practices, and legacy risk. This review works best as a short cross-functional working session (quality, EHS, supply chain, and manufacturing). A strong outcome looks like this: every fluid has a clear owner, a defined use case, current documentation, and a simple control plan that matches how the process actually runs on the floor. Inventory fluids by process : Confirm the full list of metal removal fluids, cleaners, corrosion preventatives, forming fluids, and specialty chemicals. Inventory accuracy : Confirm product names, SKUs, and locations match purchasing and quality records. Documentation access : Confirm Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and supporting technical documents are current and easy to retrieve. Program alignment : Document which fluids are tied to specific customers, specifications, or approvals. Control practices : Define targets, monitoring cadence, and what triggers corrective action. Legacy risk : Identify older fluids that may be misaligned as requirements change. Learn More From Quaker Houghton For aerospace quality, EHS, manufacturing, and supply chain teams looking to reduce compliance risk without slowing production, Quaker Houghton Inside Sales can help align fluid selection with documentation and control expectations. Explore the aerospace portfolio at store.quakerhoughton.com/aerospace , or start with products such as HOCUT® 795 B and QUAKERCOOL® 8013 . Support can include organizing fluid documentation for audits, mapping fluids to program requirements and aerospace OEM approvals (when applicable), and defining practical control plans that match shop-floor reality. Contact Us Shop Now FAQs Why are aerospace manufacturing fluids so heavily regulated? Aerospace manufacturing fluids are heavily regulated because they affect controlled processes and workplace safety requirements. Fluids can influence surface condition and downstream steps such as cleaning, coating, sealing, bonding, or corrosion performance. Fluids also require hazard communication and safe-handling controls through current Safety Data Sheets (SDS). As a result, fluids often sit at the intersection of quality, EHS, and customer program requirements. Which EHS regulations most commonly affect aerospace metalworking fluids? EHS requirements that affect aerospace metalworking fluids depend on where an organization operates and ships products. In the EU/EEA, REACH (Registration, Evaluation, Authorization and Restriction of Chemicals) and the CLP Regulation (Classification, Labelling and Packaging) influence chemical management and hazard communication. Many aerospace customers also maintain restricted-substance lists that add requirements beyond regulations. Current SDS access and internal screening records support audits and customer inquiries. What are the risks of using non-approved fluids on aerospace programs? The primary risks are requalification workload, audit findings, and schedule disruption. When a fluid cannot be tied to program requirements, teams often validate performance and update documentation before continuing at full speed. Documentation gaps can trigger nonconformances and corrective actions during audits. Even when part quality is acceptable, approval uncertainty can delay deliveries. Why do OEM approvals matter for metalworking and process fluids? OEM approvals matter because they reduce ambiguity about what is acceptable for a specific aerospace program. Approvals (or qualification to customer requirements) provide a documented basis for material selection and help keep purchasing , quality, and manufacturing aligned. They can also reduce the likelihood of mid-program fluid changes that trigger rework or revalidation. When approvals are required , having supporting records ready improves audit readiness. How can fluid choice impact audit outcomes in aerospace manufacturing? Fluid choice impacts audit outcomes when documentation and controls are incomplete or inconsistent with stated requirements. Audits typically go smoother when records show the exact product in use, current SDS access, and how key parameters are monitored . Standardized fluids and consistent naming across purchasing , quality, and the shop floor reduce confusion. Defined corrective actions help demonstrate process stability when measurements drift. What compliance risks are hidden in legacy or long-standing fluids? Legacy fluids create compliance risk when documentation, traceability, or restricted-substance expectations are no longer current. Over time, SDS revisions, customer requirements, and internal standards can change even if a fluid continues to run well in production. If records do not clearly show product identity and current documentation, audits become harder and corrective actions increase. Scheduled reviews confirm whether legacy fluids still match program needs. What risks do changing regulations pose for legacy aerospace fluids? Changing regulations can require updated documentation, additional screening, or replacement of fluids that were previously acceptable. As chemical-management rules and customer restricted-substance expectations evolve, internal reviews may need to be repeated to maintain compliance. If changes are discovered late, organizations may need to pause usage while alternatives are evaluated. Annual reviews and per-program-change reviews reduce last-minute disruption.

title: "I hate my RPA"
body_text: When we have this banner up at conferences, I get one of two responses: “What the [pick an expletive] is an RPA?” OR “I hate my RPA.” RPAs are probably one of the most incredible disappointing pieces of software. When I say that, I don’t mean “incredibly disappointing”; I mean the most genuinely incredible in its promise and yet disappointing in its execution. Robotic Process Automation is incredible because it tackles real problems that represent a significant operational cost. Because of this, at the end of even the most middling implementation of RPA solutions you will usually find a somewhat satisfied customer. The disappointing part comes in the long tail of supporting and maintaining an RPA process. Almost every RPA implementation you come across, no matter how good, is held up by a platoon of consultants, engineers, and subject matter experts tasked with constantly triaging the many ways the process might fail. To what extent new, LLM-agent-driven “Cognitive Automation” ends up being a meaningful improvement over RPA remains to be seen. I think it’ll ultimately come down to whether the maintenance long tail is meaningfully better.

title: How Worthington Steel Supports Your Sustainability Goals
summary: Learn about our EH&S team and how they can help you better understand your emissions data, address compliance requirements, and provide support.
body_text: Introduction In today's competitive manufacturing landscape, a trusted steel partner must offer more than exceptional product quality, on-time delivery, and excellent customer service. As environmental concerns grow among regulators and consumers, sustainability initiatives have become a vital differentiator and source of long-term value. Yet for many companies, sustainability remains an ambiguous goal to achieve. Gaining expertise takes time, and pursuing it can distract from other top-of-mind business priorities. However, at Worthington Steel, a North American steel processing company, we recognize that environmental responsibility is directly tied to business success in some facets. That is why our Environmental, Health, and Safety (EH&S) team is focused not only on reducing our impact but also on providing resources to help you do the same. This blog explores how Worthington Steel supports you in achieving your sustainability objectives through practical guidance, precise data, and industry expertise. You can read it straight through or jump to sections that are most relevant to your needs. This article will walk you through the following: The Basics of Sustainabilitiy in Manufacturing What Worthington Steel Does for Our Customers What Worthington Steel Does Internally Why This Matters: Practical Sustainability, Not Greenwashing The Basics of Sustainability in Manufacturing Environmental concerns in manufacturing became a global focus in the late 20th century. As awareness grew from environmental incidents and scientific consensus, so did the pressure from government entities and stakeholders for accountability and improved practices. This led to the development of the modern ESG framework, where businesses commit to improving their impact on the environment (E), their employees and communities (S), and their governance (G). This framework expanded on its predecessor, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), which was well known to many companies at the start of environmental regulation. ESG reporting provides transparency to stakeholders and helps companies track their progress over time. However, there are no universal standards for emission calculations or certifications, making it challenging to navigate this landscape. This is where Worthington Steel's customer partnership dynamic proves to be a valuable asset. With decades of experience in the steel industry and our processes, we can provide the necessary data and answers transparently to help you make informed decisions with clarity and confidence at every step. Our EH&S team is there to help with required certifications, data dissemination, and calculations. What Worthington Steel Does for the Customer Transparent Data and Reporting As an OEM or Tier 1 supplier, you are facing growing pressure from stakeholders to account for and reduce Scope 3 emissions. To meet this, collecting accurate data is critical. That is where Worthington's EH&S team plays a role in delivering our data with detail and transparency. Worthington can provide historical emissions data by facility to help you analyze your steel sourcing over time and the direct Scope 3 emission reductions associated with us. This can help evaluate your supply chain and track progress on overall goals. Also, to include in your report are product-specific carbon profiles showing the embedded carbon per ton of steel processed at Worthington, making it easier to be detailed in your Scope 3 emission disclosures. Additionally, our team supports navigating complex compliance requirements across regions. Whether it's documentation for Clean California Steel certification to enable infrastructure bids or assisting with Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) declarations for steel shipped to the European Union, Worthington Steel can provide credible, timely information to you. Informed, Feasible Decision Making Sustainable sourcing requires more than meeting minimum requirements; it involves understanding the trade-offs between costs, availability, and environmental impacts. Navigating these considerations can be complex, particularly when balancing short-term operational needs with long-term sustainability goals. Some of our partners came to us asking about Integrated vs. Mini mills . Questions like "What would it take to reduce emissions in our steel supply?" and "What are the trade-offs in cost, product availability, and feasibility?" Our EH&S team, often in collaboration with our metallurgists and commercial teams, helps answer those questions with real data and tailored recommendations. Tools like Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) provide transparency that supports informed decision-making. For instance, EPDs can show that steel from mini mills emits around 1.1 metric tons of CO2 per ton, while integrated mills can produce roughly twice that amount. With this level of insight, procurement teams can align sourcing strategies with both operational and sustainability priorities. By providing this level of clarity, we empower our customers to make sourcing decisions that are both technically feasible and cost-effective, aligning with their strategic business goals. These insights are especially valuable for manufacturers seeking to meet aggressive 2030 reduction goals or those needing to demonstrate measurable progress to stakeholders. Sharing Progress and Driving Accountability Sustainability performance is not just a matter of internal tracking but relates to how leading companies evaluate their suppliers. Recognizing this shift, Worthington Steel actively participates in independent assessment platforms, such as EcoVadis, where our practices are benchmarked against global peers in areas including environment, labor safety, ethics, and supply chain management. We share these scores, along with our annual ESG reports, so that procurement teams and you can better understand our progress. Our most recent EcoVadis rating places Worthington Steel in the top quartile of intermediate steel processors. This score reflects our ongoing efforts to meet rigorous ESG goals, our commitment to continuous improvement, and our ability to meet customers' expectations. For our customers who may not be aware of these resources, please feel free to follow our EcoVadis account to track our environmental progress and request our records to help inform your procurement decisions. Verdict : At Worthington Steel, we're not here to push costly or drastic sustainability changes. Instead, we focus on providing clear data and practical support to help customers make informed decisions. Our goal is to help you pursue sustainability improvements that align with your business, deliver real value, and positively impact your triple bottom line. What Does Worthington Steel Do Internally? Operational Sustainability in Action: Green Star Program To effectively deliver on our promises to stakeholders regarding sustainability progress, Worthington Steel developed a plant-level initiative called the Green Star Program. Every facility is challenged each quarter to implement measurable improvements in energy efficiency, water usage, and waste reduction. These projects are not only beneficial for the environment, but they are also designed to deliver tangible operational value. In the area of energy efficiency, maintenance teams utilize diagnostics to detect and correct inefficient motors, employing tools such as vibration diagnostics and amperage monitoring. This allowed for a reduction in power consumption while extending the equipment's useful life. Water conservation efforts have also made a significant impact at our Delta facility. Updates to processes have saved millions of gallons annually and improved the quality of discharge to the Maumee River. These changes not only reduce environmental impact but also strengthen compliance and plant performance. Even in regions with unique climate challenges, we have found innovative ways to reduce waste and improve efficiency. At our Tempel Mexico facility, for example, the team developed a closed-loop system to reclaim and purify air conditioning condensation using reverse osmosis and charcoal filtration. These models exemplify resource efficiency and serve as a testament to what is possible when sustainability is approached with creativity, intention, and innovation. Transportation & Emission Efficiency Emissions associated with transportation are a key part of the environmental footprint in steel supply chains. Recognizing this, Worthington Steel has focused on identifying practical ways to improve freight efficiency without disrupting delivery reliability. A small but impactful adjustment was when the transportation team shifted from a single to a dual-coil truckload, resulting in a 60% increase in freight efficiency. This change significantly reduced emissions per ton of steel delivered, offering immediate benefits for customers working to measure and reduce their Scope 3 emissions. Verdict : We share these successes to demonstrate how targeted operational improvements can support both environmental goals and supply chain performance. Our approach is opportunistic, focusing on programs that cut costs, boost efficiencies, and minimize our environmental impact while making progress on our promises. These kinds of practical, high-return initiatives help us stay competitive, operationally strong, and sustainably focused to best support our customers. Practical Sustainability, Not Greenwashing For manufacturers in industries such as automotive, energy, and construction, the pressure to reduce emissions is real, often accompanied by cost constraints, evolving regulations, and operational complexity. In this environment, sustainability initiatives must deliver tangible value to be effective. At Worthington Steel, our approach is rooted in practicality. Rather than promoting costly or idealistic changes, we focus on providing reliable, data-driven insights that help customers make informed decisions. Our goal is to support progress in ways that align with existing business objectives and deliver meaningful outcomes over time. We view sustainability as a tool to strengthen your operations, not complicate your operations. Through steady collaboration, we are committed to helping you build a smarter, more sustainable supply chain, one decision at a time. About Worthington Steel Since 1955, Worthington Flat Roll Steel has been delivering top-quality service that enables our customers to do the same for themselves. Our steel processing capabilities serve a variety of markets, including automotive , heavy truck , agriculture , energy , construction , and many others. Our commitment to our customers' business goes far beyond supplying steel. We provide advanced materials support , buying strategies , supply chain solutions , and the highest level of customer service and collaboration. If you are interested in learning more about us at Worthington Steel, want to view our capabilities , or have a question that we can help you answer , please explore our website or call us at 1.800.944.3733. We are here to be partners for your manufacturing goals.

title: Managing and scoping React Native upgrades
summary: Learn tips and tricks for handling React Native upgrades from the perspective of Rippling’s Engineering team.
body_text: At Rippling, our journey with React Native has been a key part of building mobile applications that are fast, reliable, and feature-rich. With more than five years of experience using React Native, we've harnessed its ability to share code across platforms and enable collaboration between web and mobile engineers, allowing us to deliver seamless product integrations efficiently. The React Native community moves quickly, with frequent updates and releases. Staying up-to-date with these rapid changes is essential for maintaining the security, performance, and compatibility of our apps— Rippling Mobile and Rippling Kiosk . Initially, we upgraded every year, but we've since transitioned to semi-annual major upgrades, reflecting a more structured approach to managing the fast-paced evolution of React Native. While these upgrades can be challenging, they offer substantial benefits, such as access to new APIs, improved developer tools, and optimized performance. In this blog, we’ll take you behind the scenes at Rippling, sharing our strategies for scoping and managing React Native upgrades. From allocating dedicated resources to overcoming specific challenges, we’ll provide insights into how we balance the disruption of an upgrade with its long-term advantages, making sure our apps continue to deliver exceptional experiences for employees. Rippling’s mobile apps: A brief overview Rippling has two mobile applications, each serving distinct purposes for different user groups: App name Audience & Purpose Features Store Availability Rippling Mobile App Employees - Offers a unified platform for employees to manage various HR, Finance, and IT-related tasks. - Time and Attendance : Track work hours and attendance patterns - Payroll : View salary details and manage pay-related information - Spend Management : Expense reimbursements - Time Off : Apply for and manage leaves - Benefits : Explore and manage employee benefits Google: Play Store Apple: App Store Rippling Kiosk App Hourly employees of companies - A dedicated app for clocking in and out of shifts, ensuring streamlined time tracking for hourly workers. - Clock in/out Pin Based - Manage shifts Google: Play Store Apple: App Store Both apps undergo 200+ releases annually and integrate with more than 10 products , showcasing the scale and complexity of the systems we manage. With a mix of 53% focused on bug fixes, performance, and stability improvements, and 47% introducing new features, these frequent releases are key to maintaining app reliability and driving innovation. Over the years, Rippling has consistently embraced updates in React Native to stay aligned with the evolving ecosystem. These frequent updates and integrations highlight the dynamic nature of our mobile platform and our commitment to continuously improving the user experience, ensuring both apps remain performant, reliable, and up to date with modern development standards. Why Rippling upgrades React Native These upgrades are essential for ensuring our apps remain secure, high-performing, and aligned with the latest technology standards. Here are the key reasons why we prioritize regular upgrades, along with a look at how they’ve directly benefited our engineering efforts: 1. Access to new features: Upgrading unlocks new features and performance optimizations that directly enhance our apps. For example, during our upgrade to React Native 0.70, we saw significant improvements with the introduction of Hermes as the default JavaScript engine . This change reduced our JavaScript bundle load time by more than 50%, improving app launch speeds and delivering a noticeably smoother user experience. 2. Security improvements: With each upgrade, we ensure that our apps are protected against vulnerabilities through critical security patches. This proactive approach helps safeguard sensitive user data and meets compliance standards expected by businesses using Rippling. 3. Bug fixes and stability enhancements: New versions address existing bugs and stability issues, minimizing downtime and making troubleshooting easier. For example, during the upgrade from 0.72 to 0.73, we benefited from fixes to previously reported crashes in edge-case scenarios, leading to a more stable application. 4. Compatibility with third-party libraries: Upgrades help us maintain compatibility with the third-party libraries we rely on. As we upgraded to React Native 0.72, the improved support for TypeScript allowed us to better integrate type safety into our codebase, reducing runtime errors and making our development process more robust. 5. Support for new React, iOS, and Android versions: Each major upgrade aligns our apps with updated React versions, the latest Android and iOS operating systems, and essential development tools like Android Studio and Xcode. For example, upgrading to React Native 0.72 ensured our apps were optimized for the latest macOS and Xcode upgrades, making it easier for engineers to maintain and enhance the product. 6. Fulfilling policy requirements: The mobile app ecosystem is constantly evolving, with Apple and Google frequently updating their policies. Regular upgrades help us meet these requirements seamlessly. For instance, our recent upgrades ensured that our apps complied with the latest iOS App Store and Google Play Store submission guidelines. Failure to keep up with these updates could lead to serious consequences, including app rejection, removal from the stores, revenue loss, and damage to user trust. By staying compliant, we not only avoid these risks but also ensure the continued availability of our app, maintaining both our user base and brand reputation. 7. Future-proofing through end-of-life awareness: Staying informed about React Native’s End-of-Life (EOL) policies is vital. Running an unsupported version risks exposing apps to security vulnerabilities and integration issues with third-party libraries. Regular upgrades, such as our recent transition from 0.70 to 0.73, ensure that our apps remain compliant, secure, and easy to maintain, while also benefiting from community support and updated resources. Understanding the upgrade process Upgrading React Native isn’t just about updating a library—it’s a comprehensive process that touches multiple layers of your application. At Rippling, we recently upgraded from React Native 0.72 to 0.73 , which provides a practical example of the considerations and adjustments involved. 1. JavaScript code: One of the first steps in the upgrade was reviewing our JavaScript codebase. The new version introduced changes to APIs, requiring us to replace deprecated methods and adjust functionality. For instance, we refactored parts of our code to align with stricter type-checking enforced by the updated TypeScript version, ensuring smoother runtime behavior and reducing errors. 2. Native code: This upgrade required updates to our native Android and iOS codebases. With the new version of React Native, support for the latest iOS and Android operating systems was introduced. We adjusted files like build.gradle for Android and Podfile for iOS to ensure compatibility, enabling our apps to leverage platform-specific enhancements and policies. 3. Third-Party dependencies: Several third-party libraries we rely on, such as React Navigation and Detox needed updates to stay compatible with React Native 0.73. During the process, we resolved conflicts arising from outdated dependencies and ensured that their latest versions worked seamlessly within our app ecosystem. 4. Configuration files: Key configuration files like AndroidManifest.xml and Info.plist required minor changes to meet the latest requirements. For instance, we updated permissions and configurations to comply with the latest Android and iOS store submission guidelines, ensuring our apps met policy standards. 5. CI/CD pipelines: Our CI/CD pipelines also underwent modifications. The upgrade introduced updated build requirements, prompting us to adjust our workflows in Bitrise and GitHub Actions. This ensured that builds were efficient and aligned with the new version’s dependencies and testing frameworks. 6. Static analysis tools: As part of our commitment to maintaining high code quality, we upgraded static analysis tools like TypeScript , ESLint , and Prettier . These upgrades enabled us to use new rules and improved error detection, particularly beneficial for catching issues during the early stages of development. 7. Other development tools: We also updated our debugging tools and IDEs, such as Android Studio and Xcode , to their latest versions. These updates offered better support for React Native 0.73, improved performance during development, and provided access to new debugging features that simplified troubleshooting. Key lessons learned from the past upgrades: Plan for dependencies: Upgrading third-party libraries alongside React Native is critical to avoid compatibility issues. Test incrementally: Running tests throughout the process helped us catch bugs early and minimized disruption to ongoing development. Optimize CI/CD: Updating CI/CD pipelines early in the process ensured seamless integration and deployment once the upgrade was complete. Communicate clearly: Having one engineer dedicated to the upgrade allowed us to minimize disruption to feature development while maintaining clear communication with the broader team. By following a structured approach, we ensured that the transition was smooth, enabling Rippling Mobile and Rippling Kiosk to take full advantage of React Native 0.73’s new features and improvements. This upgrade was not just a technical necessity—it was an investment in the future scalability and performance of our apps. Adopting a gradual approach At Rippling, we've found that adopting a gradual approach is one of the most effective strategies for managing React Native upgrades. Instead of tackling the entire application at once, we break the process into smaller, manageable steps. This incremental method allows us to: Mitigate risks: Address potential issues in a controlled manner by upgrading specific features or components step by step Maintain functionality: Ensure that the application remains operational throughout the upgrade process, minimizing disruption to end users Facilitate testing and validation: Focus on smaller, isolated changes that are easier to test and validate, ensuring stability and compatibility Integrate enhancements seamlessly: Gradual upgrades make it easier to incorporate and leverage new React Native features and improvements without overwhelming the development process This approach has proven invaluable in managing complexity and delivering a more resilient application. By prioritizing stability and user experience, a phased strategy helps us maximize the benefits of upgrading while minimizing disruptions. Scoping the Upgrade Before beginning the React Native upgrade process, it’s critical to scope the changes comprehensively. This step ensures that the transition is well-planned and minimizes disruptions to your application. Here’s how we approach scoping at Rippling: 1. Reviewing the changelog Action: Analyze the official React Native changelog for all versions included in the upgrade path. Purpose: Gain a clear understanding of changes, deprecated APIs, and new features that might impact your app. Benefit: This helps anticipate the necessary modifications and plan the upgrade steps effectively. 2. Consulting the React Native blog Action : Explore the React Native blog to stay updated with announcements, insights, and detailed upgrade guides from the core team. Purpose : Gain a deeper understanding of major updates, migration strategies, and the latest features to better align your upgrade process with React Native's best practices. Benefit : Leverage expert guidance to streamline the upgrade, minimize risks, and effectively utilize new enhancements in your application. 3. Using upgrade helper tools Tools: We leverage the React Native Upgrade Helper and Expo Native Project Upgrade Helper to streamline our upgrade process. Functionality: These tools highlight the differences between the current and target versions, simplifying the identification of required changes. Using the Upgrade Helper, we can quickly pinpoint necessary code adjustments and configurations for JavaScript and Native code. Expo CNG (Continuous Native Generation) adoption : To further simplify and accelerate our upgrade process, we’re planning to adopt Expo CNG (Continuous Native Generation) soon. Expo CNG introduces an innovative approach by providing a continuous integration system that handles the generation of native code. This helps eliminate manual processes traditionally involved with managing native code changes, reducing friction and increasing the speed of upgrades. By leveraging Expo CNG, we expect even smoother native updates, quicker iterations, and better alignment with modern development practices. Adopting Expo CNG is a strategic step forward, not only improving our internal development workflows but also contributing to the Expo ecosystem. By relying on Expo’s powerful infrastructure, we can more easily manage native dependencies, reduce the risk of incompatibilities, and keep both of our mobile apps performing optimally with minimal overhead. 4. Updating dependencies Process: Audit all third-party libraries and confirm compatibility with the target React Native version. Tools: Use npm outdated or yarn outdated to identify outdated packages. Action: Check each dependency’s repository for migration guides and updates. 5. Evaluating custom code Scope: Review any custom code or patches applied to the React Native framework. Outcome: Ensure customizations align with the updated framework and plan necessary adjustments. 6. Reviewing security implications Focus: Examine security updates or requirements in the target version. Action: Verify compliance with new security practices to safeguard user data. 7. Mapping features and impact Approach: Create a detailed list of app features and identify those impacted by the upgrade. Outcome: This enables prioritization and planning for potential adjustments or testing needs. 8. Prioritizing upgrades Strategy: Tackle critical features and high-impact areas first, leaving less essential components for later phases. Result: This ensures that vital functionality remains intact throughout the upgrade process. 9. Assessing performance metrics Baseline: Gather pre-upgrade performance data to compare with post-upgrade metrics. Objective: Identify and address any regressions introduced during the update. 10. Establishing rollback procedures Plan: Document a rollback strategy to revert to the previous version if significant issues arise. Impact: This reduces downtime and ensures a quick recovery if unexpected problems occur. 11. Team communication Engagement: Involve the team in planning discussions to gather input on potential challenges. Alignment: Make sure everyone understands the upgrade strategy and their responsibilities. By following this structured approach to scoping, we ensure a smoother upgrade process that minimizes risks, reduces surprises, and prepares the team to tackle challenges effectively. This proactive planning lays the foundation for a successful React Native upgrade while maintaining stability and performance. Compatibility with third-party libraries: A major risk One of the most significant risks we encountered was third-party library compatibility. Many of our dependencies were not immediately compatible with the latest React Native version, which introduced delays and additional troubleshooting steps. To manage this risk: Early compatibility assessment: We reviewed each dependency and checked for compatibility information or recent updates on their repositories. Temporary forks and custom patches: For critical libraries lacking official updates, we created temporary forks and modified the code ourselves. This helped us keep the upgrade on track while waiting for library maintainers to release official patches. Exploring alternatives: When certain libraries seemed unlikely to receive updates soon, we researched alternative solutions that were compatible with the new React Native version. Dependency compatibility is a crucial risk factor during upgrades. Approaching it with a proactive strategy minimized disruptions, allowing us to maintain the app’s functionality throughout the process. Effort and team Involvement in RN upgrades At Rippling, the RN upgrade process typically requires six to eight engineer weeks , depending on the scope and complexity of the upgrade. The effort is primarily led by a single dedicated engineer who drives the upgrade process while collaborating with other team members as needed. This ensures minimal disruption to ongoing feature development, as most of the team continues to focus on their regular work. Cross-functional input is occasionally required to address issues in specific product modules and to verify that the upgrade does not introduce regressions. Automating the upgrade process At Rippling, we prioritize efficiency in our upgrade workflows by automating key steps of the React Native upgrade process. Leveraging tools and scripts helps us streamline the process, reduce manual effort, and minimize errors. Some of the tools we use or recommend include: React Native Upgrade Helper : A community-driven tool that provides a detailed, side-by-side comparison of changes required for upgrading to a specific version of React Native. This helps ensure we don’t miss critical updates in configuration files or dependencies. Expo Native Project Upgrade Helper : For projects using Expo, this tool offers a similar experience by highlighting the necessary adjustments to seamlessly transition to newer versions. Custom scripts: We have developed in-house scripts to automate repetitive tasks, such as dependency checks and static analysis tool upgrades, ensuring a consistent approach to upgrades. By automating much of the upgrade process, we save time, reduce the risk of human error, and ensure a smoother transition to the latest version. This approach also frees up our engineering resources to focus on delivering new features and improving user experience. Maintaining backward compatibility At Rippling, ensuring backward compatibility during React Native upgrades is a critical part of our process. We aim to provide a seamless experience for our users, avoiding disruptions or issues when transitioning to the upgraded version. Here’s how we approach this: 1. Reviewing breaking changes: We meticulously analyze the React Native release notes to identify potential breaking changes. Any APIs, modules, or configurations impacted by the upgrade are flagged for review and adjustment. 2. Feature flags: We implement feature flags to isolate new features or changes. This allows us to enable or disable specific functionalities dynamically, minimizing user impact if issues arise. 3. Testing strategy: Automated testing: Comprehensive test suites ensure that existing functionalities are validated against the updated React Native version. Manual testing: Edge cases and user-specific scenarios are manually tested to catch any discrepancies not covered by automation. By prioritizing backward compatibility, we uphold our commitment to delivering a reliable and user-friendly experience while embracing the improvements offered by new React Native versions. Debugging Debugging during the upgrade process is a crucial phase that requires a meticulous and systematic approach. As you implement updates, you may encounter unexpected behaviors or errors that disrupt functionality. To efficiently address these issues, use a combination of tools that offer powerful debugging capabilities and insights into your app's performance. Debugging tools Flipper (GitHub: Flipper ): All-in-One Tool (Deprecated). Previously used for debugging at Rippling, but we have since transitioned to other tools listed below Network inspection : Proxyman (Website: Proxyman ). Used to inspect and analyze network requests and responses, ensuring the app communicates correctly with external services UI inspection : React DevTools UI Inspector (Documentation: React DevTools UI Inspector ). Helps analyze the app's UI hierarchy and components JavaScript debugging : Chrome Debugger for efficient JavaScript debugging, helping identify issues in the logic and execution flow Performance monitoring : Performance Monitor (Documentation: React Native Performance Monitor ). Used to track and address performance bottlenecks in the app Clearing caches Sometimes, issues arise from outdated cache files during the upgrade process. Clearing various caches can help resolve these problems and ensure consistency: Metro Bundler Cache : Run npx react-native start --reset-cache to reset the Metro cache. npm Cache : Use npm cache clean --force to clear the npm cache. Yarn Cache : Clear the Yarn cache by running yarn cache clean. Android Build Cache : For Android, run cd android && ./gradlew clean to clear the build cache. iOS Derived Data : Navigate to ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData and delete the contents to clear Xcode's derived data. Community resources In addition to the tools mentioned, consulting community resources such as forums and GitHub issues (e.g., React Native and Expo repositories) can provide valuable insights into common upgrade-related pitfalls. By systematically debugging and clearing caches, you can address issues more efficiently, ensuring a smoother transition to the new version of React Native and enhancing your app’s stability and performance. Testing and validation Thorough testing and validation play a critical role in ensuring the success of your React Native upgrade. A comprehensive testing strategy should include both automated and manual testing to ensure stability and a seamless user experience. Automated testing To cover all critical functionality, we utilize various tools in Rippling testing suite: Static checks : We use tools like ESLint for linting, unimported to detect unused code, TSC for type errors, and checks for cyclic dependencies to maintain code quality. Screenshot testing : We leverage react-native-owl (GitHub: react-native-owl ) for automated screenshot testing, ensuring that the UI remains consistent across updates. Unit testing : For isolated function and logic testing, Jest is our go-to framework. It helps us verify that individual components and functions are working as expected. End-to-end testing : Detox (GitHub: Detox ) is used for runtime end-to-end tests, ensuring the entire flow of the app works seamlessly in real-world scenarios. Manual testing In addition to automated testing, we perform manual testing to validate the overall user experience and identify any potential regressions that may have been missed by automation. This combination of tools and methods ensures that your app remains stable and that users enjoy a smooth, error-free experience after the upgrade. Continuous integration and deployment At Rippling, Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Deployment (CD) pipelines are an integral part of our overall development workflow. These pipelines automate key steps like building, testing, and deploying applications, ensuring a seamless, reliable, and efficient process for all code changes, including React Native upgrades. This approach minimizes manual intervention, reduces the risk of errors, and maintains consistent application stability and performance. We use Bitrise as our primary CI/CD platform, which allows us to: Automate builds : Every code change, including React Native version upgrades, is automatically built to ensure compatibility and identify potential issues early in the process. Run tests : Bitrise integrates with our testing framework to execute unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, ensuring that the application maintains functionality and performance post-upgrade. Streamline deployments : Upgraded builds are deployed automatically to testing environments, and eventually to production, following successful validation. By leveraging Bitrise, we maintain a consistent upgrade workflow that enhances both Rippling Mobile and Rippling Kiosk apps' stability and performance. This automation accelerates the deployment process, ensuring that users benefit from the latest features and improvements with minimal delay. Phased rollout to reduce risk of breaking changes At Rippling, we adopt a phased rollout strategy to ensure a smooth and stable transition during React Native upgrades. This dual-approach strategy minimizes risks by tailoring deployment methods based on the type of changes being introduced. For native changes , we utilize the native phased-release capabilities offered by the App Store and Google Play. These allow us to roll out updates to a percentage of users incrementally, ensuring that any issues with native components, such as updates to Android or iOS code, configuration files, or third-party libraries, can be identified and addressed early. This approach is particularly useful for updates that cannot be handled via OTA tools, such as changes to native modules or platform-specific optimizations. For JavaScript-only changes , we leverage OTA (Over-The-Air) updates using tools like Expo Updates . Previously, we relied on CodePush for OTA releases, which allowed us to gradually release changes to user subsets. With the transition to Expo Updates, we’ve gained access to a more robust feature set: Flexible rollout controls: Gradual deployments to targeted user groups help us monitor app behavior and collect feedback before broader rollouts. Enhanced rollback mechanisms: Issues can be quickly mitigated with streamlined rollback capabilities, ensuring minimal disruption for users. Improved analytics: Enhanced tracking provides detailed insights into performance and user engagement during phased rollouts. Cross-platform efficiency: Expo Updates simplifies OTA updates for both Android and iOS platforms, keeping the user experience consistent. By combining these two strategies, we ensure that Rippling Mobile and Rippling Kiosk apps maintain high performance and stability during updates. This approach enables us to balance the speed and flexibility of OTA updates with the rigor and safety of native phased releases, ensuring minimal disruption while maximizing the benefits of React Native upgrades. Monitor for issues Post-deployment monitoring is a critical step in the React Native upgrade process. Even with comprehensive testing, some issues may only surface in the production environment. At Rippling, we rely on a robust monitoring stack to proactively identify and resolve problems, ensuring a seamless user experience after each upgrade. Error monitoring with Sentry : We use Sentry to track both JavaScript and native crashes . This allows us to capture detailed error reports, including stack traces and user context, helping us quickly pinpoint and resolve issues. Sentry’s real-time alerts ensure that our team is notified immediately when a problem arises, reducing response time. Logging and performance tracking with Datadog : For deeper insights into application behavior, we leverage Datadog . It helps us track logs, monitor application performance, and identify bottlenecks or anomalies in the system. With Datadog, we gain visibility into critical metrics like API response times, memory usage, and user interactions, enabling us to maintain high performance and stability. By combining Sentry and Datadog, we create a comprehensive monitoring ecosystem that covers all aspects of our application, from JavaScript code to native modules. This proactive approach allows us to catch and address potential issues before they impact our users, ensuring a smooth post-upgrade experience for both Rippling Mobile and Rippling Kiosk apps. Update documentation After completing the upgrade, we at Rippling ensure that all internal documentation is updated to reflect the changes. This allows future developers to easily understand the rationale behind the upgrade, as well as any new features or modifications. Keeping the documentation thorough and up-to-date is key to maintaining project continuity and facilitating a smoother transition for anyone working on the codebase in the future. Conclusion Upgrading your React Native application may seem daunting, but with the right approach, it can be a seamless process that unlocks significant benefits. At Rippling, we've honed our strategy to ensure smooth transitions while minimizing disruptions. Here’s a recap of key takeaways: Adopt a gradual approach: Break the upgrade into smaller, manageable steps to reduce risks and improve stability. Scope effectively: Clearly identify necessary changes and prioritize them to focus on what's most impactful. Leverage automation: Use tools like Bitrise and Expo Updates to streamline upgrade, testing, and deployment processes. Maintain backward compatibility: Safeguard existing functionality to ensure a seamless experience for all users. Prioritize testing and validation: Implement robust testing strategies, including automated and manual testing, to identify issues early. Utilize CI/CD pipelines: Integrate upgrades into your CI/CD processes for efficient testing and reliable deployment. By adopting these practices, you can not only minimize the challenges associated with upgrading but also maximize the value of new features, security patches, and performance enhancements that each new React Native version brings. Upgrading isn’t just a maintenance task—it’s a critical step toward keeping your application future-proof and delivering the best possible experience to your users. We're hiring engineers! title: Local Legends: Animal Crackers, Where Customers Become Family
summary: Watch Local Legends: Animal Crackers Where Customers Become Family and explore more insights from Brixmor on retail, redevelopment, and community. Check out the latest from our blog.
body_text: Community-driven retail builds lasting loyalty When small businesses create meaningful connections with their customers, they do more than sell products. They become part of the community. Animal Crackers in Plano, Texas is a clear example of how a locally owned retailer can grow into a destination that keeps generations coming back. For more than 30 years, Animal Crackers has built a loyal following by delivering a warm and personal shopping experience. Customers are not just shoppers. They are treated like family. From knowing customer preferences and sizes to going above and beyond with thoughtful service, the team has created a place where people feel recognized, valued, and excited to return. Located in an open-air retail center, the store benefits from strong visibility, steady foot traffic, and a walkable environment that encourages discovery. Combined with a bright and playful atmosphere, a curated mix of products, and a beloved shop dog, Animal Crackers offers more than retail. It creates a memorable local experience. This is what happens when the right tenant meets the right retail environment. In this video, you will see: • How personalized service builds multi-generational customer loyalty • Why community first retailers drive repeat visits and strong engagement • The role of open-air retail centers in increasing foot traffic and discovery • How local ownership creates deeper customer relationships • Why experiential shopping encourages customers to keep coming back Why it matters: Community rooted businesses like Animal Crackers do more than operate in a center. They elevate it. Their ability to create connection, loyalty, and consistent traffic strengthens overall performance and supports long term value for the entire retail environment.
